opener_concept: Squash/sugar-jug dilution: pour out half a jug (2 spoonfuls per litre) and a child can see the glass holds 1 spoonful but is still 2-per-litre strong. Names amount=moles, strength=concentration, and the core titration insight that a sample shares the flask's concentration but has fewer moles. Leads to n = c x V.
walk_ritual: Every walk follows equation -> unit conversion box (cm3 -> dm3, its own catchable box) -> substitute -> compute -> check that restates the answer WITH UNIT. Completion boundary (phase:substitute) leaves the known-side set-up pre-worked and the student computes the unknown side plus the reverse check.
tier_ladder: Bronze = single equation (n=cV, c=n/V, V=n/c, n=mass/Mr, unit convert). Silver = one titration with unit conversion + mole ratio. Gold = multi-step (mass->flask conc->sample->ratio->titre conc, or mass-back-calculation). Bank matches the ladder; no reordering needed.
